poolReview.rationale: Real reversal with intermediate morphology delivers a surprising understandable payoff.

candidates.subject: The jellyfish that can reverse its life cycle
candidates.novelty: Adult medusa becomes an attached polyp, rather than a smaller juvenile jellyfish.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: Primary tissue experiments and barcode-confirmed modern research distinguish morphology from molecular hypothesis.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: An adult medusa can reorganize through a cyst into polyps that bud new medusae; reversible development does not mean death is impossible.
candidates.visualPotential: Continuous original medusa → regressing form → cyst → stolon → polyp colony → new medusa.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: How can an adult animal return to a different earlier form?
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original deterministic translucent anatomical illustration and stage morphing, existing local af_heart.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Owner-selected marine biology; no category whitelist or visual alternation.
candidates.comparison: Owner selected topic; evidence selects a stage-accurate framing.
limitations: Not invulnerable or proof of endless survival.
Ten repeats in2011 were unidentified Turritopsis sp.; no species transfer.
Molecular pathways remain candidates, not proven causal controls.

curiosityReview.honestPremise: The jellyfish that can reverse its life cycle
curiosityReview.coldAudienceReason: An apparent impossibility resolves into a different body plan and a reusable mental model of development.
curiosityReview.storyRoute: Beautiful medusa → normal budding → stress → loss of medusa form → cyst and cell identity → stolon/polyps → new medusae → mortality → reversible development.

truthBoundary.rationale: Reverse development, not reverse time or invulnerability; cyst-based route illustrated without claiming every reversal follows identical timing.

opportunityJudgment.rationale: Strong observed morphology with honest limits makes transformation the explanation.
